title: Barcelona to Mallorca
subtitle: Two days in Gaudí's city, then a slow week at Camp de Mar
summary: Two packed days on foot through Montjuïc, the Gothic Quarter and Gaudí's Barcelona, an early flight to Mallorca for five slow days at Zafiro Palace Andratx in Camp de Mar, then a last night back in Barcelona.

intro: We gave Barcelona two packed days and saw as much of it as we could on foot: Montjuïc, La Rambla and the Gothic Quarter, El Born, Passeig de Gràcia and the port on the first day, then Sagrada Família, the Passion Tower, Sant Pau and Park Güell on the second.

Then we took an early flight to the island for five slow days at Zafiro Palace Andratx on Mallorca's southwest coast. We booked a single tour for the week and left every other day open, then flew back to Barcelona for one last night in the city before heading home.

days_plan.label: Day 1
days_plan.title: Montjuïc, the Old City and the port
days_plan.text: We landed, dropped our bags and walked straight out the door: a loop from the hotel on Montjuïc down through the medieval core, up to Passeig de Gràcia and back by cable car.

items.text: Land in Barcelona; customs and immigration, then a taxi or Uber to the hotel
Check in at the InterContinental Barcelona (if the room isn't ready, they'll hold the bags). It has a rooftop pool and bar.
Montjuïc on foot, 5–10 minutes from the hotel
Palau Nacional: the palace built for the 1929 International Exhibition, now the National Art Museum of Catalonia. Even without the museum, the Oval Hall and the terrace views are worth it.
Magic Fountain of Montjuïc: free and 1929-era. The water, music and light shows only run in the evening; by day it's mostly dormant.
Uber or taxi to La Boqueria (10–15 minutes)
La Rambla and the Gothic Quarter on foot, one of the prettiest walks in the city
La Boqueria, the huge historic food market, then down La Rambla
Plaça Reial: a 19th-century neoclassical square with palm trees, busy terraces and street lamps by a young Gaudí
Gothic Quarter: medieval lanes, Roman ruins, tapas bars and artisan shops; a good place for lunch
Plaça Sant Jaume, home of the town hall, and Barcelona Cathedral
El Born to the Arc de Triomf on foot
Mercat de Santa Caterina, the El Born neighbourhood and the Gothic basilica of Santa Maria del Mar
Parc de la Ciutadella, on the site of a former military citadel
Arc de Triomf: the red-brick gateway to the 1888 Universal Exposition, then a stroll down the palm-lined promenade
Taxi to Casa Batlló (about 25 minutes on foot otherwise), then walk Passeig de Gràcia: Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside, plus 150+ designer boutiques in historic buildings
Uber or taxi to Port Vell, the oldest part of the port, rebuilt for the 1992 Olympics: Maremagnum, IMAX Port Vell and Europe's largest aquarium
Port Cable Car up to Montjuïc for views and photos, then walk back to the hotel
Back to the hotel to relax
Dinner at La Gastronómica Tapas, about a 15-minute walk from the hotel (reserved on TheFork)
Walk back and bed

days_plan.tip: If the cable car line is long, skip it and taxi back; if you're running early, add Montjuïc Castle (check it's still open).

days_plan.label: Day 2
days_plan.title: Gaudí, Modernisme and the view from the top
days_plan.text: Timed entries all morning, a hidden Art Nouveau campus at lunch, Park Güell in the afternoon and a late dinner at Casa Amàlia 1950.

items.text: Taxi to Sagrada Família, aiming to be at the entrance by 9:30

Sagrada Família tour. The 9–10 AM Quiet Hour means the basilica is silent when you walk in, and by 10:00 the morning sun lights up the blue, green and yellow windows of the eastern Nativity facade. We spent the first hour on the east side of the nave before the sun climbed.
Climb the Passion Tower: elevator up, then a very narrow, winding spiral staircase down
Museum and gift shop under the Passion facade; from the basement museum a small window looks down on Gaudí's tomb in the crypt
Quick bite nearby: TuscaniaLab on the plaza, Buenas Migas or the Mercat de la Sagrada Família

Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau (1:30 PM tickets, a 10-minute walk), the world's largest Art Nouveau complex and a UNESCO site: a former hospital built 1905–1930 as a garden city of light, air and green space

Our quick route: the Administration Pavilion's pink vaulted ceilings and stained-glass staircase, the Central Courtyard and the coloured dome of the Sant Salvador Pavilion, a photo of the circular glass Operating Theatre, then out through the white-tiled underground tunnels
Uber to Park Güell
Park Güell
Optional drink and a bite: Restaurant Terra Mía, Comida de Olla or Bodega La Riera
Taxi to Bunkers del Carmel (Turó de la Rovira), only if the sky is clear. It's just a high point, but the panorama is spectacular.
Back to the hotel to freshen up, with a drink at the rooftop bar
Drinks nearby first, then Uber or taxi to dinner
Dinner at Casa Amàlia 1950

tips.title: Dress for Sagrada Família
tips.text: Shoulders and knees need to be covered, and hats and caps come off inside.

tips.title: Go early for the light
tips.text: The 9–10 AM Quiet Hour is calm, and around 10:00 the sun streams through the Nativity facade's windows. Spend the first hour on the east side of the nave before the sun climbs.

tips.title: Head to the tower early, with a coin
tips.text: Lines for the Passion Tower elevator back up, so start walking about ten minutes before your slot. Bags go in free lockers at the base, which need a 1-euro coin.

tips.title: Check which cable car you want
tips.text: There's more than one cable car option in Barcelona, so check which one goes where you want. The Port Cable Car runs from the waterfront up to Montjuïc; if the line is long, take a taxi instead.

tips.title: Getting to Port Vell
tips.text: Give your driver Moll de la Fusta, the wharf, as the address.

tips.title: Watch the weather for Bunkers del Carmel
tips.text: It's only worth the trip on a clear day; otherwise the hotel rooftop pool is a fine alternative.

tips.title: Eating near Park Güell
tips.text: Avoid anywhere with "Güell" in the name.

tips.title: Check opening hours
tips.text: If you want to add Montjuïc Castle at the end of a day, check its closing time first.
